parole.testo: From a Turkic language, probably from Cuman, see Turkish below. Ultimately from Proto-Turkic *baltu, see more there.
From a Turkic language, from Proto-Turkic *bas- (“to press”). Compare Turkish bas- (“to press”).

From the obsolete verb bocsánik + -at (noun-forming suffix), from a Turkic language before the times of the Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin (at the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries). Ultimately from Proto-Turkic *boĺ.

From a Turkic language before the times of the Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin (at the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries), from Proto-Turkic *bas-. Compare Turkish basmak. Probably related to Udmurt busturgan, presumably of Chuvash origin.
Probably borrowed from a Turkic language before the times of the Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin (at the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries), ultimately from Proto-Turkic *bāka.

parole.significato: to endure, to stand, to bear, to cope with something
parole.testo: From a Turkic language, ultimately from Proto-Turkic *buyur-. Compare Chuvash пӳр (pür) and Turkish buyurmak.

Borrowed from a Chuvash-type Turkic language before the times of the Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin (at the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries). From Proto-Turkic *bẹĺčig (“cradle”). Probably borrowed from a Turkic language, ultimately from Proto-Turkic *bulan (“elk”). Compare Bashkir болан (bolan, “deer; elk”).

Borrowed from a Turkic language before the times of the Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin (at the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries). parole.significato: rheum (in the corner of the eyes), sleep
parole.testo: From a Turkic language, from Proto-Turkic *čalp-. Compare Turkish çapak (“rheum”).
From a Turkic language. Compare Turkish yoğurmak, from Proto-Turkic *yugur- (“to knead”).

parole.significato: sand (rock that is ground more finely than gravel, but is not as fine as silt, forming beaches and deserts and also use…
parole.testo: A very old borrowing from a Turkic language, compare Southern Altai кумак (kumak, “sand”), Yakut кумах (kumax, “sand”), from Proto-Turkic *kum (“sand”).
Borrowed from a Turkic language, ultimately from Proto-Turkic *uruk.

parole.significato: a concept relating to the temporal dimension
parole.testo: Probably borrowed from a Chuvash-type Turkic language before the times of the Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin (at the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries), ultimately from Proto-Turkic *öd (“time”) and cognates with Karakhanid اُذْ (öδ, “time”), Southern Altai ӧй (öy, “time”), Turkish öğle
First attested in 1222. Probably borrowed from a Turkic language. From Proto-Turkic *kïrguy (“kite, falcon”).
Borrowed from a Turkic language, compare Turkish güvercin (“dove, pigeon”), from Proto-Turkic *kȫker- (“to turn blue”), from Proto-Turkic *kȫk (“blue”).

Borrowed from a Chuvash-type Turkic language before the times of the Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin (at the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries). Compare Tatar колмак (qolmaq), Bashkir ҡомалаҡ (qomalaq) and Chuvash хӑмла (hămla). From Proto-Turkic *kumlak.
Borrowed from a Chuvash-type Turkic language before the times of the Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin (at the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries), ultimately from Proto-Turkic *kapïrčak.
Borrowed from a Turkic language before the times of the Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin (at the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries). Ultimately from Proto-Turkic *kēp (“form, image”).
From a Turkic language, from Proto-Turkic *kīndik. Compare Kipchak kindik, Tatar кендек (kendek, “navel”).

Borrowed from a Chuvash-type Turkic language before the times of the Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin (at the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries). Ultimately from Proto-Turkic *kebrüč (“ash tree”), compare Chuvash каврӑҫ (kavrăś, “ash tree”).
Borrowed from a Turkic language before the times of the Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin (at the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries), ultimately from Proto-Turkic *okï-.

Probably borrowed from a Turkic language before the times of the Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin (at the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries). From Proto-Turkic *sep- (“to scatter, sprinkle”).
From a Turkic language, from Proto-Turkic *sekü (“stone bench, pedestal”). Compare Turkish seki (“stone seat”).
From a Turkic language, possibly from Proto-Turkic *sek- + -ik. Compare Turkish sekmek.
Borrowed from a Turkic language. Ultimately from Proto-Turkic *siŋek.

parole.significato: grape (a small, round, smooth-skinned edible fruit, usually purple, red, or green, that grows in bunches on vines of ge…
parole.testo: Borrowed from an indeterminate Oghur Turkic language before the times of the Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin (at the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries). Ultimately from Proto-Turkic *yidgelek (“berry”), cognate with Chuvash ҫырла (śyrla).

parole.significato: yellow (of a yellow hue, the color between green and orange on the spectrum of light)
parole.testo: From a Turkic language, ultimately from Proto-Turkic *sārïg (“yellow, white”), via an intermediate form *siarg-a (note *-ï- elided). Compare Turkish sarı, Khakas сарығ (sarığ) and Chuvash шурӑ (šură).
From a Turkic language, ultimately from Proto-Turkic *sāŕgan (“carp; snake, dragon”). Compare Cuman sazagan, Kipchak sazağan (“dragon”), Turkish sazan (“carp”).

parole.significato: to endure, tolerate, bear, put up with, brook
parole.testo: From a Turkic language, most likely Oghur (compare to Old Chuvash *tör-, tür-), from Proto-Turkic *töŕ- (“to bear, endure, suffer”). Probably a word loaned during the Magyars’ presumed part in the Onogur tribal alliance.

Borrowed from a Turkic language before the times of the Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin (at the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries), from Proto-Turkic *arpa. The sense “bacterial infection of the eye” is perhaps a calque of scientific Latin hordeolum (“stye”), from Latin hordeolus.

parole.significato: intellect, brains, mind, reason, judgment, intelligence, sanity, remembrance (the content of one's head in a figurative…
parole.testo: First attested in 1372. From a Turkic language before the times of the Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin (at the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries), ultimately from Proto-Turkic *es. Compare Chuvash ас (as).

From Turkic *aɣïl; compare Chuvash ял (jal). Borrowed before the times of the Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin (at the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries). Ultimately from Proto-Turkic *āɣïl.

parole.significato: heifer (young female cattle, i.e. young cow)
parole.testo: Borrowing from a Turkic language, from Proto-Turkic *in-gek (“cow”). Compare Chuvash ӗне (ĕne), Old Turkic 𐰃𐰤𐰏𐰛 (ingek) and Turkish inek.

parole.significato: to grow crazy, to become mad
parole.testo: From Old Hungarian *aβril (“to go in circles, be dizzy”), borrowed from a Turkic language before the times of the Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin (at the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries), ultimately from Proto-Turkic *ebir- (“to turn”).
